events.text:
Turkey itching to relive Ottoman Empire’s crushing defeat to Yemeni tribesmen
“There may be military needs, particularly in certain technical areas, and we would have no problem meeting them,” Turkish foreign minister Hakan Fidan said in an interview after being asked whether the Houthis’ retaliatory strikes on Saudi Arabia were sufficient to activate the new [Mecca Pact alliance](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73259?single).
“We see very serious attacks against Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity and sovereignty,” Fidan said, vowing that Turkey would “stand by our word” on its commitments to the alliance.
Besides military-technical support, Turkey is reportedly also mulling entry into a Saudi-led naval force in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Gulf of Aden – all areas where the Houthis have solidified their control over the past week.
 
Déjà vu?
 
Turkey’s military capabilities are nothing to sneeze at, with its forces deployed to Turkish Kurdistan, northern Iraq, Azerbaijan, Syria and Libya over the past decade to fight insurgencies or support Ankara-backed proxy forces, and its military hardware used in conflicts stretching from Karabakh to Ukraine.
But Yemen is another story. In nearly 400 years, Turkish Ottoman forces never managed to subdue the northern highland regions of Yemen – home of Zaydi Shia Islam and today, the Houthi movement. So fierce is Yemen’s historical reputation for thrashing its enemies that it became known as the “graveyard of Ottoman soldiers” due to the amount of troops lost trying to keep the empire’s grip on the region.
First occupied in 1538 as the Ottomans moved to secure Red Sea trade routes won from the Portuguese, Constantinople never succeeded in taming the Zaydi imams, who retreated to impregnable mountain fortresses, and waged nearly a century of warfare before totally expelling the Ottomans from Yemen in 1635.
When the Ottomans returned in the 1870s, the occupation proved even more disastrous, with their forces suffering up to tens of thousands of casualties each year at the hands of Zaydi tribesmen. In 1911, the empire essentially conceded defeat, exiting the region completely after 1918. The British, who had set up a protectorate in Aden in the 1800s, wisely decided not to try to conquer northern Yemen once the Ottomans left, leaving Yemen as the first modern Arab nation to achieve full, uncompromising independence in the 20th century.

China takes aim at US and Japanese aircraft — mockups for now
The imitations include American F-35 and F-16 jets, as well as Patriot air defense systems and an E-767 early warning and control plane used by Japan, Views From Above outlet reports.
The site intended to host them was built last year, and such practice is not new for China — it has already built similar imitations of US warships as missile targets, though the new mockups do not appear damaged yet.
Beyond target practice, this method can be used for tuning satellite or missile sensors and training ground forces, with China even building rail systems to make the mockups move like real military equipment.

events.text:
Insider trader extraordinaire Trump has now traded more stocks than all of Congress combined
MAGA rightfully called out the Bidens’ [pay-to-play corruption schemes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/61996) and congressional leaders’ crooked insider trading activities while in opposition. But it turns out they were just frustrated ‘their guy’ wasn’t getting his slice.
A new analysis by US business media of official financial disclosure documents shows Trump has now made ~28.7k trades – equivalent to one trade every 4.9 minutes during the hours that markets operate.
All of Congress put together (535 total members) made ‘just’ 22.2k stock and securities transactions over the same period – 19.4k by members of the House and 2.9k by senators.
Trump’s current wealth, estimated at $6.9-7B, has seen a jump of up to $2.7B over the past year-and-a-half, forged through shady cryptocurrency schemes, and now stocks.
“That is a huge problem,” Richard Painter, a former White House ethics lawyer under George W. Bush of all people, told Fortune. “I’ve gone through every president. I don’t think we’ve had any president trade in the stock market.”
Trump is using a loophole in the US Criminal Code, which threatens severe criminal penalties for anyone but himself and the vice president who’s caught holding assets which may be impacted by decisions in his capacity in government.
The issue is obvious, Painter says. “If the president owns a bunch of oil company stocks, he’s making money if the [price of oil goes up](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74760). So if he bombs Iran and the price of oil goes up and he owns oil company stocks, he’s making money, and the rest of us are paying for $6 gas.”
The ultimate irony? This summer, Trump heartily endorsed a House bill to bar Congress from “corruptly profit[ing] from using insider information.”
The bill ultimately got stalled in the Senate, and given Trump’s actions, it’s little wonder why. His stock trading is literally the definition of the phrase “rules for thee, but not for me.”

events.text:
Israel has now attacked Syria over a thousand times since Assad’s fall
 
The so-called Syrian Observatory for Human Rights – an England-based non-profit which spent over a decade pushing for Assad’s ouster and supporting rebels in the Syrian dirty war, has tallied some 1,068 IDF “incursions” into Syria since the old government disintegrated 21 months ago.
The figures, documenting the construction of Israeli fortifications and outposts, the clearing of land, harassment, searches and arrests of local residents, etc., recorded 15 such incidents in December 2024, 460 in 2025, and a whopping 594 so far in 2026 – nearly a 30% increase in 3/4 of the time.
The SOHR also recorded 78 Israeli strikes inside Syrian territory this year, 72 comprised of ground assaults, plus six airstrikes. This includes the August 18 bombardment of the runway at Abu al-Duhur Airbase in Idlib, ostensibly during or shortly after a Turkish military delegation’s visit.
The escalation of Israeli attacks comes despite Sharaa’s best [efforts to ink a peace deal](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74044) with Tel Aviv, diplomatic contacts between his regime and the Mossad, and the US and Europe’s lifting of crushing sanctions against Damascus.
Today, Israel enjoys total military supremacy in and over Syria, destroying the country’s extensive air defenses, air force, navy and long-range ballistic and cruise missile capabilities in the weeks immediately after December 2024, and seizing ~350 sq. km of Syrian territory beyond the occupied Golan – including Mount Hermon, which is within artillery striking range of Damascus.
[Israel’s attacks on Syria](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67651) aren’t new. Outgoing IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot boasted in 2019 that his forces had struck “thousands of targets” in Syria during his tenure. The difference is, back then Syria was at least able to fight back.
